code_requests.change: Conventional flame look. (a) The fb_grad core-rim temperature uses the 3D sample radius lq. With kf = 14/fb.w the flame is opaque within ~7% of its radius, so only lq of about 0.9-1.0 (0.78 T) is ever seen and the 1.30x core is invisible. code_requests.change: stem_density(): the axis blend makes the axis core the tallest and densest part of the crown. The fallback top is 0.8 h, but most jet tops with jet_amount=1 are 0.5-0.7 h, and jets squeezed into the w_ax transition wedge reach about 1.1 h. A false-colour render (stem red, head green) showed this core poking out as the lit tan pillar or spike. Fix: blend to the azimuthal MEDIAN instead. top_j = mix(stem.x + (stem.y-stem.x)*mix(0.92, 0.62, jamt2)*(0.85+0.3*lf), top_j, smoothstep(0.05*r, 0.45*r, rx2)), and for the density use jet = mix(mix(0.55, 0.40, jamt), jet, w_ax). Better still, evaluate the jet noise at a fixed minimum radius (cs from p.xz + 0.45*r*dir) so wedges do not converge on the axis.

code_requests.change: For conventional flames (fb_grad > 0), derive tloc from the ray's impact parameter to the fireball centre, b = length(cross(ph - fb.xyz, rd))/fb.w, instead of the 3D radius lq. The opaque surface always sits at lq ~ 1, so the 1.30 -> 0.75 core-to-rim gradient is never seen. Use tloc = T*mix(1.30, 0.75, smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, b)). Also clamp the soot mix (fb_shape.w) to [0,1] before mix(), and make the soot one-sided (skin *= smoothstep(-0.2, 0.5, q.y)).
